summary: Cross-surface fix for the Chapman-1933 mischaracterization and the unsourced one-signed 5-25/5-30 nT standard-physics range, reusing the WIN-010 (EXP-684-rev2, c18-approved) wording. 30 exact-text patches over sections.json (part1, part1b, part4, part5, part6, part8, part9, part10), kill-shots.json KS-005 (4 fields) and predictions.json PRED-095 (tldr, detail_reasoning). No verdict changes. Frozen predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json not touched.
kernel_of_truth: Chapman (1933) really is the founding paper: he correctly worked out that an eclipse cutting E-layer ionization should weaken the Sq currents and leave a ground magnetic signature, which is exactly the mechanism modern models (Ashour-Chapman, Meza et al. 2022) use. The review was right that the globe does not predict 0 nT. What it got wrong is the history and the number: Chapman judged the 1933 data did NOT show the effect (and leaned toward an F-layer Sq source), and no source has been found for a one-signed 5-25 nT Z range. The non-discrimination argument does not need either claim: the dome magnitudes are the 2017 Boulder globe-Earth measurement rescaled by coverage (shared arithmetic, section 4.2.5), which is a stronger and fully sourced point.

chapman_1933.abstract_finding: Infers the magnetic effects an E-layer Sq system would show in an eclipse; expresses the opinion that eclipse observations show no regular effect of that type, so Sq is probably not produced in the E-layer; final decision to await further observations.

chapman_1919.title: The solar and lunar diurnal variations of terrestrial magnetism
chapman_1919.note: This is the venue part10 bibliography wrongly attaches to the 1933 paper.

kim_chang_2018.note: Abstract not available via Crossref/Semantic Scholar (publisher-elided). Content description (~200 records, ~100 INTERMAGNET observatories, 1991-2016, effect grows with magnitude, strongest at 30-50 deg magnetic latitude) is carried from the c18-approved WIN-010 detail_evidence, not re-read this run.

meza_2022.note: Abstract re-read via Semantic Scholar this run ("strikingly accurately" quote confirmed). BOU dX ~+10 nT / dZ ~+3-4 nT are figure-read values from monitor/analyst/analysis-records/win010-c17-rev2-verification-20260929.json literature_checks.meza_2022; labelled approximate in the patch text.

five_to_25_nT.note: No paper located that gives a 5-25 nT (or 5-30 nT) standard-physics range; Chapman 1933 gives no number. Same untraced-number pattern as Erratum 1 E-3 / B1-M-001.

design_decisions: Section 4.2.6 (p4-426) is a public pre-registered commitment that quotes "up to about 25 nT". Rewriting it after the August 2026 event would be exactly the goalpost-moving we criticise in the dome. Patch P13 therefore ANNOTATES it (dated note) and leaves the commitment text unchanged; the eclipse results work (EXP-687) evaluates against it as written. Decider/curmudgeon: please keep this as an annotation, not a rewrite.

part10 #p10-3 changelog entry ("peer-reviewed literature shows 5-20 nT") is a historical version note; left unchanged as a record. If the operator wants, add a later changelog line pointing at this correction instead.
part8b #p8b-3-eclipse-layers quotes "the Chapman mechanism (90+ years old)" as WIN-068 verdict text; not false (1919 or 1933 both >90 years) and it is a quotation, so no patch.
PRED-TIER-1 "~10-30 min" recovery-time wording and PRED-072 (Chapman & Bartels 1940 for Sq) are correct and untouched.
Replacement wording reuses WIN-010 integrated text ("an effect Chapman worked out ... in 1933", Kim & Chang 2018 confirmation) so the surfaces agree with the c18-approved WIN.
counter_argument_considered: A defender of the old text could say "5-25 nT is a fair order-of-magnitude summary and dropping it weakens the non-discrimination point". Rejected: the number is untraceable, the Z sign at Boulder is positive while the dome predicts negative values, and the arithmetic (baseline x coverage x FSF) argument already shows non-discrimination without any literature range. Keeping an unsourced number on 12 surfaces is the bigger credibility risk, and a defender who opens Chapman 1933 gets an easy rebuttal on every one of them.
adjacent_out_of_scope: WIN-025 (wins.json index 24): "5-30 nT" unsourced range in detail_evidence/detail_verdict_text/tldr_evidence, and tldr_evidence says eclipse variations "have been known since Chapman (1919)" (1919 is the Sq paper, not eclipses). Same defect class; recommend a follow-up ISS.

WIN-068 (wins.json index 69): detail_verdict_text/tldr_verdict say Kim & Chang (2018) confirmed the effect "across 39 eclipses". WIN-010 (c18-approved) describes Kim & Chang as ~200 records from ~100 observatories, 1991-2016; "39 eclipses / 207 observations" is the dome's own ensemble description. Possible conflation; needs a check of the paper before any edit. Recommend folding into the same follow-up ISS.
